response.query: Which regulatory pathway will we target (EUA, 510(k), IVDR), what core analytical and accelerated/real‑time stability studies are needed for submission, and what target cost‑per‑test and supplier redundancy plan will de‑risk manufacturing?
response.answer: Target EUA for emergency use; IVDR for in vitro diagnostics; stability studies include accelerated and real-time; aim for cost-per-test under $50 and supplier redundancy for critical components.

results.title: Medical Devices; Laboratory Developed Tests
results.content: The Food and Drug Administration is issuing a final rule to amend its regulations to make explicit that in vitro diagnostic products (IVDs) are devices under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) including when the manufacturer of the IVD is a laboratory. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA, the Agency, or we) is amending its regulations to make explicit that IVDs are devices under the FD&C Act including when the manufacturer of the IVD is a laboratory. For example, FDA stated in the “Framework for Regulatory Oversight of Laboratory Developed Tests (LDTs)” draft guidance that “FDA intends to *continue to enforce* investigational device requirements under 21 CFR part 812 for all clinical investigations of LDTs that are conducted under clinical protocols that require institutional review board approval” (Ref. 38). The proposed rule seeks to amend the FDA's regulations to make explicit that IVDs are devices under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, including when the manufacturer of the IVD is a laboratory.
